source.title: Critical initialisation for deep signal propagation in noisy rectifier neural networks
source.authors: Arnu Pretorius; Elan Van Biljon; Steve Kroon; H. Kamper

record.tranche_reason: Tests how initialization affects signal propagation and training in noisy ReLU networks, using autoencoder loss and signal statistics rather than the classification-error measure in the claim.
record.gate_note: The experiments test dropout-initialized ReLU networks on MNIST and CIFAR-10 using an identity autoencoder task and squared reconstruction loss. Figure 6 also measures training and validation loss across depths and dropout rates; the reported text describes the trend, but does not give exact plotted values. No classification-error or CIFAR-100 result is reported.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4 using initialization comparisons in fully connected noisy ReLU autoencoders, reconstruction-loss trajectories, signal-propagation experiments and theoretical analysis. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct but overstates the empirical trainable-depth conclusion. The authors find that noise-aware initialization stabilizes forward propagation and permits initial training at depth 200 where He initialization fails. Noise still degrades correlation information and performance at criticality. They explicitly acknowledge that successful deep training conflicts with their theoretical trainable-depth predictions, leaving that discrepancy unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Uses dropout-aware initialization in noisy ReLU autoencoders and measures reconstruction loss and signal propagation; the claim versions describe classification error or other initialization settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization (critical versus He), dropout rate, depth, dataset, learning rate and optimizer; the depth/noise relationship is reported for training and validation loss.
record.problems: The real-data training experiments use an identity autoencoder with squared reconstruction loss rather than classification error. Exact Figure 6–10 plotted values are not provided in the text. The authors limit their theoretical scope mainly to fully connected feed-forward ReLU networks with a recursive dense-layer/noise-layer architecture.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and model-size or training-duration conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity shortcuts, very deep tanh initialization and Fixup.

Orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, very deep tanh networks, orthogonal convolution kernels and 10,000-layer training. The training comparisons establish early loss reduction rather than a numerical speedup or final convergence.
Stability-limit learning rates, curvature changes, catapult dynamics and edge-of-stability training.
Batch-normalization comparisons, higher learning-rate tolerance attributable to normalization and Fixup.

missing.what: Real-data forward-variance sweeps through 1,000 layers at p = 0.6 compare 25 initialization variances from 0.1 to 2.5. Critical variance 1.2 preserves propagation; off-critical choices cause underflow or overflow, with predicted numerical-instability depths matching the empirical boundary.

Theoretical and simulated results distinguish additive from multiplicative noise. The authors report no critical initialization for nonzero additive noise under their criterion, whereas multiplicative noise permits noise-dependent initialization sigma_w^2 = 2/mu_2 with zero biases.

At critical initialization, the theoretical backward error-variance multiplier is D_(l+1)/(D_l mu_2), implying vanishing errors at constant width for multiplicative noise. Growing successive widths by mu_2 preserves this variance under the stated mean-field assumptions.

Simulated correlation dynamics and depth scales show faster loss of input-correlation information with stronger noise, despite critical forward variance. The theoretical depth-scale fit deteriorates near zero noise.

record.verdict_notes: He initialization under dropout is not a separate challenge or scope limitation for V4: its failure is the expected outcome when initialization omits the injected noise. The theoretical backward-propagation results assume independently sampled forward and backward weights. Exact loss values cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and the size and training-duration conditions.
Two-layer teacher-student networks and spurious local minima.
Plain versus residual shortcuts, batch normalization, and the Fixup comparison.
The experiments concern noisy ReLU networks and dropout, not the cited plain tanh or convolutional-network settings; they do not compare orthogonal and Gaussian weights or test 10,000-layer networks.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness, and the catapult or edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: ReLU network with dropout, critical initialisation
rows.operation_detail: Trained a denoising autoencoder with dropout using squared reconstruction loss; critical dropout initialization.
rows.baseline: He initialisation under the same reported settings
rows.value: Networks initialised at criticality seem to remain trainable even up to a depth of 200 layers (loss starts to decrease over five epochs).
rows.locator: Supplementary Material C.5, Figure 8 and accompanying text
rows.note: The text summarizes the plotted result across the tested optimizers and learning rates; exact loss values are not stated.
rows.check: The evidence establishes that loss begins decreasing over five epochs at depth 200, not convergence to low loss or a quantified speed advantage.

rows.subject: ReLU network with dropout, He initialisation
rows.operation_detail: Trained a denoising autoencoder with dropout using squared reconstruction loss; He initialization.
rows.baseline: Critical dropout initialisation under the same reported settings
rows.value: Networks using the “He” initialisation become untrainable irrespective of the chosen learning rate or optimisation procedure.
rows.locator: Supplementary Material C.5, Figure 8 and accompanying text
rows.note: The authors attribute the failure to unstable forward signal propagation; Figure 10 shows activation variance for the first forward pass.
rows.check: He initialization ignores dropout's variance amplification here. Its failure while dropout-aware initialization trains supports V4's initialization dependence; it is not a reversed effect.

rows.measure: Training loss and validation loss by depth and dropout
rows.value: The authors report a relationship between depth and noise in network loss, and say even modest noise can limit performance.
rows.note: Exact plotted values are not stated. The authors say 6ξc tracks the depth beyond which relative validation-loss performance becomes poor more than it tracks training loss.
rows.check: Correct critical initialization to sigma_w^2 = 2/mu_2 = 2p, with zero biases. Separate training from validation loss: the theoretical depth boundary tracks validation performance better. The reported performance deterioration does not establish a hard maximum trainable depth.

source_check.correct: Critical initialization: σw²=2/μ₂=2p, σb=0; actual per-weight variance is σw² divided by the preceding layer width. state=cannot_determine for V4's joint signal-and-gradient preservation claim: this initialization preserves forward variance, while the theory predicts vanishing gradients at constant width.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3, critical initialization derivation and equations (6), (10); Section 4, Figure 6; Supplement C.4.
source_check.problem: The critical-variance formula is wrong, and poorer performance under forward-only preservation does not establish an incomplete effect under V4's joint preservation condition.

relationships.condition: Fully connected ReLU autoencoders with dropout retention probability p = 0.6, depth 200, on MNIST and CIFAR-10
relationships.reason: R1–R6 show early loss reduction with dropout-aware initialization, failed training with He initialization, and stable versus overflowing forward variance. The comparator failures support initialization dependence.
relationships.display_finding: Dropout-aware initialization preserved stable forward variance and reduced loss early, whereas He initialization produced overflowing variance and failed training.

tranche.reason: Initialization comparisons in noisy ReLU autoencoders use reconstruction loss and propagation analysis to address initialization-dependent trainability.

source_check.notes: Depth-200 evidence establishes loss beginning to decrease over five epochs. The authors acknowledge disagreement between observed training and theoretical depth scales; 6ξc tracks relative validation performance better than training loss.

statements.correction: Critical initialization preserves forward variance; training and validation performance depend on depth and noise; constant-width backward error variance theoretically vanishes with multiplicative noise. Joint signal-and-gradient preservation is not established in these experiments.
statements.problem: The empirical and theoretical descriptions are accurate, but the limits_scope interpretation does not follow for V4, which already requires preserving gradients as well as signals.
